b: When we celebrated our first Thanksgiving, we were poor college students, 1,600 miles from home.
I’ll never forget how proud we felt to host Dave Tricky, a fellow student, and his girlfriend for our first Thanksgiving. (Yes, that’s his real name. I soon learned the trick was on me.)
We were becoming ‘real’ adults. My bride was 19. I was 20.
We moved our tiny kitchen table to the ‘larger’ living room. It sat uncomfortably close to the front door to accommodate the crowd.
I ceremoniously stood as the ‘man’ of the house, blade in hand, ready to carve the bird. It was one of life’s great moments.
But the knife didn’t slice into tender breast meat. It was solid. I poked the blade around. The whole damn turkey was bone. I had purchased a BONE TURKEY!
Dave and his girlfriend probably stopped at a fast-food joint on their way home. It was a perfect Thanksgiving for vegetarians.
I carried the bone-bird to our cramped kitchen, defeated, to scavenge any remains. (We could use even sparse leftovers.) That’s when I flipped the bird over.
Two succulent breasts stared me in the face.
We cooked the bird upside down!
Humble yourself before a turkey humbles you.
You have more than you think.
Sometimes a different approach changes everything.
One day, if you keep learning, you’ll laugh at how ignorant you used to be.
*This post was originally published on Nov. 22, 2012. Occasionally, I repost it this time of year.
